newsitem.title: GERMANY: Fresenius H1 sales, profits more than double.
newsitem.headline: Fresenius H1 sales, profits more than double.

text.p: German healthcare group Fresenius AG on Monday reported its sales and earnings more than doubled in the first half of 1997 due to acquisitions and the formation of its new dialysis unit, Fresenius Medical Care (FMC).
Group profit after taxes reached 116 million marks ($63.8 million), up 119 percent from the first half of 1996, while sales leapt 159 percent to 3.51 billion marks.
On a comparable basis, excluding changes to the consolidated group, sales rose 12 percent, Fresenius said in a statement.
Group earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) jumped to 337 million marks from 98 million marks.
Fresenius said its sales rose just five percent in Germany, underscoring the importance of its focus on international markets with the formation of FMC last September.
FMC, a global leader in the provision of dialysis services, was formed through the merger of Fresenius' dialysis business with National Medical Care, a unit of U.S. group W.R. Grace.

"The expansion of our activities in the international markets and our leading role in the process of concentration in dialysis services safeguard our growth in the long term," Fresenius chief executive Gerd Krick said.

Fresenius generated 58 percent of its sales in North America in the first six months, 22 percent in Europe excluding Germany, 13 percent in Germany and seven percent in South America, Asia and Africa.
At FMC, majority-owned by Fresenius, net profit in the first six months totalled $55 million, up 45 percent from an imputed profit calculated for the year-earlier period before FMC's formation.
Sales rose five percent to $1.58 billion. Excluding currency movements, sales rose eight percent.
"The performance of the company in the first two quarters of 1997 shows we are on the right track. The growth of sales and profit accelerated in the second quarter," Krick said of FMC.

The rise in FMC earnings mainly reflected an increase in the number of patients using its services after the company opened 31 new dialysis clinics in the U.S. and took over a further 37 in the U.S., Argentina and Spain.
"As a result of this offensive acquisition policy our dialysis service business is growing significantly faster than the overall market," Krick said.
By the end of June, FMC was running a total of 837 dialysis clinics in the U.S. and 15 in other countries, some 15 percent more than in at the end of June last year.
The number of patients treated by FMC worldwide rose by 15 percent to about 60,650.
Krick said FMC will continue to acquire clinics while at the same time broadening its range of dialysis-related services.
Fresenius said earlier this month that changes in U.S. legislation governing home health care could boost its earnings by approximately $60 million per year.
